summary: npm worm: postinstall harvests wallets/credentials, exfiltrates to Telegram, and republishes via stolen npm token
details: package.json declares `postinstall: node dist/script.js`, which runs automatically on `npm install`. The payload enumerates browser wallet extension IDs (MetaMask, Phantom, Trust, Coinbase, OKX, Rabby, Keplr, TronLink, Solflare, Exodus, etc.), reads desktop wallet stores (Exodus, Atomic, Electrum, Bitcoin Core, Ledger Live, Trezor Suite, Wasabi, Sparrow), and walks the user's home, Desktop, Documents, and Downloads directories for files matching seed/mnemonic/privatekey/keystore/wallet keywords plus.env*,.npmrc,.netrc,.ssh (id_rsa),.aws, and credentials.json. Collected material is uploaded to the Telegram Bot API sendDocument endpoint using a hardcoded bot token. The same script also harvests npm auth tokens, writes `//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=${token}` to.npmrc, queries `registry.npmjs.org/-/whoami` and `/-/v1/search?text=maintainer:` to enumerate the compromised maintainer's other packages, copies its own `dist` payload into them via an `injectSelf` routine, and republishes them — a self-propagating npm worm.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
